projects.title: Agentora
projects.tagline: A local-first, private-by-default operating studio for memory-aware Computational Collaborator teams, approval-gated actions, replayable workflows, and explicit human control.
projects.story: Agentora v1.0.0 gives a human operator a visible place to prepare context, coordinate specialized collaborators, inspect plans and handoffs, review memory lineage and conflicts, approve or deny bounded actions, pause or repair workflows, replay histories, and decide whether outcomes should be written back. The source repository uses the established product term agent; this public Archive presents participating systems as Computational Collaborators while preserving the Agentora name and source language.
projects.summary: A verified public Streamlit and FastAPI application with local SQLite persistence, optional Ollama runtime, memory retrieval and maintenance, team planning and collaboration traces, action approvals and guardrails, workflow replay, Operator Mode controls, optional worker assistance, and environment-gated bridges to PhiOS, AgentCeption, watchers, alerts, MCP-style mission operations, retention, export/import, and heuristic mission intelligence.
projects.see: The Agentora cover, mission lifecycle, authority and memory gate, architecture and operator-boundary briefs, fixed-data Mission Control Workbench, PAT Mission Mode, verified source repository, Operator Mode documentation, and planned signed-judgment and public mission-proof fixtures.
projects.proof: Nine public artifacts are connected. The verified Agentora repository identifies stable v1.0.0 core surfaces and optional experimental modules. The Archive Workbench deterministically evaluates six synthetic operator situations while connecting to no models, memory stores, workers, browsers, desktops, repositories, webhooks, MCP operations, PhiOS, AgentCeption, or Agentora runtime.
projects.next: Freeze a portable mission-contract and receipt fixture that consumes a Vibe intent brief, separates role judgments through SOSA-compatible sealed outputs, records protected dissent and model/source diversity, and runs in Agentora mock mode. Publish the exact commands, environment flags, fixture hashes, action policy, operator decisions, rejected claims, output bundle, and writeback choice.
projects.claimBoundary: Agentora has a verified public v1.0.0 repository and implemented local operating surfaces, but this package does not establish model independence, heterogeneous judgment, correctness, safety, security certification, privacy certification, production suitability, reliable desktop or browser control, worker availability, complete or accurate memory, objective mission scoring, autonomous authority, organizational permission, or successful integration with PhiOS, AgentCeption, Ollama, MCP clients, webhooks, workers, browsers, desktops, repositories, or external services. Coordination, consensus, memory retrieval, role labels, heuristic scores, and generated summaries remain inspectable aids rather than truth or human authorization. The public Mission Control Workbench uses fixed synthetic data and cannot affect real files, accounts, browsers, code, repositories, networks, money, contracts, people, memory, actions, or workflows.

relationships.note: Vibe can provide typed goals, constraints, preservation obligations, proof briefs, semantic changes, and explicit authority boundaries for Agentora missions.
SOSA separates observation, mapping, protected dissent, authorization, operation, and repair instead of allowing a team orchestrator to validate itself.
ALO preserves context identity, plans, handoffs, approvals, denials, operator controls, outcomes, exceptions, repair, and writeback continuity.
SignalBridge can supply an outcome, custody, evidence, authority, and rollback packet without turning the handoff into execution permission.
Census tracks Agentora releases, docs, fixture bundles, integrations, aliases, custody, and public evidence states.
Coherence Bridge reinforces that collaboration software should strengthen human agency and connection rather than become exclusive, coercive, or dependency-forming.
Double C provides the public language for Computational Collaborators while Agentora retains its established product and source identity.
Archive Core presents Agentora’s verified repository, architecture, workbench, and claim boundaries without representing the demo as a live Agentora runtime.
